BiblicalUsage: Lêʼâh is the name of Leah, a wife of Jacob. In Genesis 29:16, "And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder [was] Leah"; and in Genesis 29:25, "it [was] Leah: and he said to Laban". In Genesis 29:31, "And when the LORD saw that Leah [was] hated".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Leah is the Bible's proof that God sees the unloved — Jacob loved Rachel more, but the Lord opened Leah's womb and gave her sons. I hold that her story is for everyone who has felt second-best: God does not overlook the tender-eyed and the passed-over.
